column3: NASB follows the critical text; it reorders “the ninth hour, the hour of prayer.”
NASB renders the imperfect “were placing” as “used to set down.”
NASB renders “was asking” as “began asking.”
NASB renders “having looked intently” as “fixed his gaze.”
NASB renders “giving heed” as “give them his attention.”
NASB follows the reading without “rise up,” which the critical text includes in brackets.
NASB follows the critical text; “having taken” is rendered “seizing.”
NASB renders “leaping up” as “with a leap.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “to beg” and renders the imperfect as “used to sit.”
NASB follows the critical text; “being called” is rendered “so-called.”
NASB follows the critical text; “godliness” is rendered “piety.”
NASB follows the critical text with “God” once; it renders “having adjudged” as “when he had decided.”
NASB renders “a man a murderer” as “a murderer.”
NASB renders “Author” as “Prince” and adds “a fact.”
NASB adds “of Jesus” and “it is”; “complete soundness” is rendered “perfect health.”
NASB renders “brothers” as “brethren” and adds “did.”
NASB renders “foretold” as “announced beforehand” and restructures the clause.
NASB moves “in order that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord,” which opens v. 20 in the Greek, into this verse; “turn again” is rendered “return.”
NASB begins after the clause moved to v. 19; it follows the critical text (“appointed”).
NASB follows the critical text; “from the age” is rendered “from ancient time.”
NASB follows the critical text; “listen” is rendered “give heed.” The quotation is in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text; “out from” is rendered “from among.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “likewise.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “It is … who.” The quotation is in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text without “Jesus”; it adds “ways.”
